lines: Opens the demo transport, which plays a scripted demonstration over the top of the rack, moving the pointer and working the controls as a person would
Note — the module does nothing until a script is chosen: press the top row of the panel, which opens the list of scripts and then names the one loaded
Note — with no script loaded the top row reads Self test, and running plays a built-in test rather than a demonstration
Note — scripts are markdown files kept in the DreamerDemo folder inside Rack's own user folder, newest edit first in the list, and a few examples are put there the first time the list is opened
Note — the thirteen rows on the panel are drawn as one widget rather than as separate controls, so none of them can be clicked for a help note of its own; what each does is written below
Note — the top row names the loaded script and opens the list, and Reload reads that file again after it has been edited
Note — Patch opens the patch the script names, the way the File menu would, so a correction made to it can be saved straight back over the file
Note — Run starts the demo and then reads Stop, which halts it with the rack left as the demo made it; pressing it again reads Reset and puts your own patch back
Note — Restart plays the script again from its first step, Back moves one step backwards and Step performs the next step alone, the last two leaving the demo stopped
Note — Rate cycles the playback speed through 0.75x, 1x, 1.5x and 2x
Note — Voice speaks the narration aloud, Badges draws the gesture marks over the controls the demo touches, and Captions shows the narration card; each is lit while it is on
Note — Record arms a screen recording rather than starting one: capture begins when a run starts and ends when it stops, and it needs macOS 13 or newer
Note — the path of a finished recording is put on the clipboard and shown in a message once the file is written
Note — Hide takes the transport window off the screen while a demo runs, so it is out of the picture being recorded
Note — the transport window carries Run, Back and Step and can be dragged anywhere; the rest of the controls stay on the module's panel
Menu — Show the runner — puts the transport window back on the screen if it has been closed
Menu — Write a port index — writes a file naming every port of every module in the rack, so that a cable recorded as a port number can be read back as a name; it takes a few seconds
Menu — Write a patch report — writes a description of the rack as it stands, walking the modules and the cables between them
Menu — Restore a saved patch — lists up to forty earlier saves of the rack, newest first, and loads the one chosen after asking; the rack it replaces is gone
Menu — Show the saved patches — opens the folder those saves are kept in
Menu — Keep the patch report up to date — rewrites the patch report every 15 seconds, on the same beat as Rack's own autosave
Demo.notes: This is our own plugin and everything above comes from its source. The module has no parameters, inputs or outputs at all, so nothing on it can be clicked for help except the title band, which is why every fact is a Note. The thirteen panel rows are drawn by one custom widget, ControlColumn, with no ParamWidget per row, so they are unreachable by a click for help even though they can be pressed. The six menu item names are the literal strings passed to createMenuItem and createBoolPtrMenuItem in DemoWidget::appendContextMenu.
